annotation.title_clean: Four Degree of Freedom Robotic Arm; An Ethical Analysis of Automation and Employment in the Manufacturing Industry
annotation.title_en: Four Degree of Freedom Robotic Arm; An Ethical Analysis of Automation and Employment in the Manufacturing Industry
annotation.venue: University of Virginia Libra (Online Archive of University of Virginia Scholarship)
annotation.summary_en: Undergraduate capstone abstract pairing the engineering of a four-DOF handwriting robotic arm with an STS literature review of manufacturing automation's labor effects (polarization, deskilling, reduced job satisfaction). It recommends proactive upskilling during deployment and human-centered, augmenting design.
key_provisions_or_claims: Automation hollows out mid-skill industrial roles, producing a barbell labor market
Shifting workers to passive screen monitoring lowers job satisfaction
Organizations should integrate proactive upskilling into technology deployment
Engineers should design systems to augment rather than replace human capability
Low-cost 4-DOF arm with cycloidal reducers and closed-loop control achieves repeatable handwriting
